stories.headline: Alibaba sues the Pentagon to exit US 'Chinese military company' blacklist

key_facts.fact: Alibaba filed a lawsuit on Tuesday, June 23, in federal court in San Jose, California, against the US Department of Defense, seeking removal from a blacklist that designates it a company supporting China's military.
key_facts.excerpt: In a lawsuit filed on Tuesday in a district court in San Jose, California, the Hangzhou-based company said the Pentagon had added Alibaba to a list of companies that allegedly aid the People's Liberation Army without providing substantial evidence or explanation.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon placed Alibaba on its 1260H list, calling it a 'military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base' over its regulatory ties to Beijing; Alibaba called the designation 'arbitrary and capricious' with 'no basis in fact or law.'
key_facts.excerpt: The defence department put Alibaba on the so-called 1260H list, saying the firm was a 'military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defence industrial base'... Alibaba pushed back, claiming the determinations 'have no basis in fact or law'.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba argued the move violates constitutional due process and its First Amendment free-speech rights; the suit notes its shareholder base is dominated by US institutions including J.P. Morgan, Citigroup and BlackRock.
key_facts.excerpt: The designation also restricts the companys' ability to retain lobbying firms in the U.S., which the lawsuit argues violates First Amendment rights. Alibaba said in its suit that it's a publicly traded e-commerce and cloud-services provider with a diverse shareholder base dominated by major American financial institutions including J.P.Morgan, Citigroup, and BlackRock.

key_facts.fact: Under the designation, starting June 30 the Pentagon cannot enter new contracts with listed firms; the rule also restricts US contractors that share a lobbyist or law firm with a blacklisted entity.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the designation, beginning June 30, the Pentagon can't enter into new contracts with designated companies or their controlled subsidiaries. The designation also restricts the companys' ability to retain lobbying firms in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon expanded its blacklist this month to include other major Chinese tech names such as Baidu, BYD, Nio, Unitree Robotics and TP-Link; China retaliated on Monday with export controls on ten US defense and rare-earth firms.
key_facts.excerpt: China retaliated against the blacklist on Monday, imposing export controls on ten U.S. companies involved in defense and rare earths mining. The feud tests bilateral relations after President Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping met in Beijing last month.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Tag, an agentic AI teammate that lives inside Slack

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude Tag on June 23, 2026, a product that embeds Claude inside Slack as a persistent, shared teammate that anyone on a team can delegate work to by typing @Claude.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Tag is a new way for teams to work with Claude. We're starting on Slack, which Claude can join as a team member. Grant Claude access to selected channels, and connect it to whichever tools, data—and even codebases—you choose.

key_facts.fact: Claude Tag is available in beta for Claude Enterprise and Team customers and replaces the existing 'Claude in Slack' app, which will be retired (administrators have 30 days to opt in to migration).
key_facts.excerpt: It's available today in beta for Claude Enterprise and Team customers... Claude Tag replaces the existing Claude in Slack app. To migrate, administrators can opt in within 30 days.

key_facts.fact: When assigned a task, Claude Tag breaks it into stages, executes them using whichever connected tools it has access to, retains context and memory across channels, and can act proactively in an 'ambient' mode.
key_facts.excerpt: When assigned a task, Claude Tag breaks it into stages and works through them using whichever tools it has access to... the more notable feature is an ambient mode that proactively jumps into conversations to keep teams updated.

key_facts.fact: The product runs on Claude Opus 4.8, the model Anthropic released less than a month earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: The product runs on Claude Opus 4.8, the model Anthropic released less than a month ago.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is offering launch credits to drive adoption: $25,000 worth of credits for Enterprise customers and $2,500 for Team customers, applicable only to Tag usage in Slack; the old Claude-in-Slack connector leaves service on August 3.
key_facts.excerpt: Enterprise customers who add Tag to Slack will get $25,000 worth of credits, while Teams customers will get $2,500... the existing connector will leave service on August 3.

stories.headline: Engram exits stealth with $98M to build a learned memory layer for AI

key_facts.fact: Engram emerged from stealth on June 23, 2026 with $98 million in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners and Neo, plus angels including Wiz CEO Assaf Rappaport, OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy and AI/robotics researcher Pieter Abbeel.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram, the company building the learned memory layer for AI, emerged from stealth with $98M in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners, Neo and notable angels and advisors including Assaf Rappaport, co-founder and CEO of Wiz, Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI, and Pieter Abbeel.

key_facts.fact: The round values Engram at $600 million; the company has just 13 employees and was founded in October 2025 out of Stanford University's AI lab, led by CEO Dr. Dan Biderman.
key_facts.excerpt: The American startup Engram... has completed a $98 million funding round at a $600 million valuation... 'We founded the company last October directly out of Stanford University's AI lab,' Biderman, who serves as the company's CEO, told.

key_facts.fact: Engram builds models that study an organization's data in advance to form a compact, continuously improving memory, which it says matches or outperforms frontier models while using just 1-10% of the tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram compresses that knowledge into reusable model memory that matches or outperforms frontier models while using 1-10% of the tokens. The AI gets smarter the more you use it, and you own the memories.

key_facts.fact: Engram has a partnership with Microsoft to test its models within Microsoft 365, including a commitment to GPU capacity across Dapple and Azure, aimed at making enterprise AI more efficient and context-aware.

stories.headline: US FCC's AWS-3 auction raises $3.5B to fund ripping out Huawei, ZTE telecom gear

key_facts.fact: The FCC said on June 23 that its AWS-3 spectrum auction, its first in four years, concluded with winning bids totaling more than $3.5 billion across 200 licenses after 72 rounds.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Communications Commission's first spectrum auction in four years concluded Tuesday, with bids totaling more than $3.5 billion. The agency re-auctioned 200 licenses in the AWS-3 bands.

key_facts.fact: Up to $3.3 billion of the proceeds will repay a Treasury loan used to fund the FCC's 'Rip and Replace' program, which reimburses smaller carriers for swapping out gear from Chinese firms Huawei and ZTE.
key_facts.excerpt: The FCC said in a release that up to $3.3 billion of the auction's proceeds would be used to pay back a Treasury loan taken out to fund its 'Rip and Replace' program... The program reimburses smaller carriers for swapping gear from Chinese firms Huawei and ZTE out of their networks.

key_facts.fact: Seventeen bidders qualified, including AT&T, EchoStar, T-Mobile, Verizon and SpaceX; winners were not immediately disclosed and will be named in a later public notice.
key_facts.excerpt: Seventeen qualified bidders, including AT&T, EchoStar, T-Mobile, Verizon and SpaceX, participated in the auction. The winners aren't being revealed right away.

key_facts.fact: Rip and Replace was created by a 2021 law with $1.9 billion in funding, but the FCC estimated removal would cost $4.98 billion, leaving carriers with partial reimbursements; as of last week 42% of recipients had completed replacement.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency previously estimated removing the Chinese equipment would cost $4.98 billion, but Congress only approved $1.9 billion before deciding to hold the auction... 42% of federal funding recipients have completed replacement and disposal of all Chinese equipment.

key_facts.fact: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said 'FCC auctions are finally back' and that the agency is on schedule to auction at least 100 MHz of upper C-band spectrum by July 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: 'After years on the sidelines, FCC auctions are finally back,' FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement... The FCC said in its release that it was 'on schedule' to sell off at least 100 megahertz in the upper C-band by July 2027.

key_facts.fact: The deal builds on a first program of record signed in June 2025, under which Harmattan delivered 1,000 Sonora units within six months; the DGA confirmed receipt of that batch on January 30, 2026.

stories.headline: Krea releases open weights for its Krea 2 image model under a custom license

key_facts.fact: On June 23, 2026, AI creative-tools startup Krea released the open weights of its Krea 2 image model as two checkpoints, 'Krea 2 Raw' (an undistilled base for fine-tuning) and 'Krea 2 Turbo' (a fast distilled version), available for download on Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: Krea is hoping to change that trend by opening up the weights to its new frontier AI image model Krea 2 as two versions, 'Krea 2 Raw' and 'Krea 2 Turbo'... Both models are available for public download on Hugging Face.

key_facts.fact: Krea 2 is built on a Diffusion Transformer scaled to 12 billion parameters trained from scratch; the Turbo variant renders native 2K-resolution images in roughly 2 seconds using an 8-step inference pipeline, among the fastest open or proprietary image models.
key_facts.excerpt: At the technical core of the release sits an architectural framework built entirely from scratch: a Diffusion Transformer scaled to 12 billion parameters... Krea 2 Turbo slashes the required generation cycle down to just 8 inference steps... in approximately 2 seconds.

key_facts.fact: The Krea 2 Community License lets individuals and small companies use the weights royalty-free but requires firms with more than 50 seats to pay for an enterprise license, and mandates all deployers implement content classifiers to block illegal, NCII, CSAM or defamatory outputs.
key_facts.excerpt: a custom license that requires firms with more than 50 seats to pay for Enterprise usage, and mandates all users of any size to implement technical safeguards to prevent the generation of illegal materials, non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), child sexual abuse material (CSAM), or defamatory assets.

key_facts.fact: Krea, founded in 2022 in San Francisco, has raised $83 million in disclosed venture funding (backers include Andreessen Horowitz and Bain Capital Ventures) and surpassed 30 million users across 191 countries as of June 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: an aggregate $83 million in disclosed venture capital funding from major VCs including Andreessen Horowitz and Bain Capital Ventures... The company's user base surpassed 30 million individuals across 191 countries as of June 2026.

stories.headline: Mistral releases OCR 4 with bounding boxes and confidence scores across 170 languages

key_facts.fact: Mistral released OCR 4 on June 23, 2026, a document-intelligence model that returns bounding boxes, typed-block classification (titles, tables, equations, signatures) and inline confidence scores alongside extracted text, supporting 170 languages across 10 language groups.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing Mistral OCR 4, featuring bounding boxes, block classification, and inline confidence scores alongside extracted text. The model supports 170 languages across 10 language groups, runs in a single container for fully self-hosted deployments.

key_facts.fact: In a blind human evaluation across 600+ real-world documents in 12+ languages, independent annotators preferred OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%.
key_facts.excerpt: Independent annotators prefer OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%, alongside the top overall score on OlmOCRBench (85.20).

key_facts.fact: OCR 4 achieves the top overall score on the public OlmOCRBench (85.20) and scores 93.07 on OmniDocBench, though Mistral cautions the aggregate automated scores are directional given known benchmark scoring limitations.
key_facts.excerpt: OCR 4 achieves the top overall score amongst the models we tested on the public OlmOCRBench (85.20)... On OmniDocBench, OCR 4 achieves a score of 93.07. We report this figure with a caveat.

key_facts.fact: OCR 4 is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages via API (dropping to $2 with a 50% Batch-API discount) and is available through Mistral Studio, Amazon SageMaker and Microsoft Foundry, with a single-container self-hosting option.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in talks to design custom chips for ByteDance using Alphawave tech

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in talks to provide custom chip-design services to China's ByteDance, parent of TikTok, according to four people familiar with the matter
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm is in talks to provide chip-design services to China's ByteDance, four people familiar with the matter said, as the U.S. company seeks to reduce dependence on the smartphone market, its biggest revenue source.

key_facts.fact: The chips would be based in part on technology owned by Alphawave Semi, a high-speed connectivity specialist Qualcomm acquired in 2025
key_facts.excerpt: The chips would be based in part on technology owned by AlphaWave Semi, a high-speed connectivity specialist Qualcomm acquired last year, two of the sources said.

key_facts.fact: The discussion involves designing video processing units (VPUs), with an eye toward starting mass production by the end of the year; ByteDance is separately developing an AI inference chip and custom CPUs

key_facts.fact: A successful deal would make ByteDance an early customer of Qualcomm's chip-design services operation; the outcome remains uncertain and ByteDance could pursue other partners

key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm is working to break into the booming data center chip market and working with customers on three kinds of chips: CPUs, accelerators for inference, and custom chips called ASICs, a fast-growing market for rivals such as Broadcom and Marvell.

stories.headline: SpaceX debuts Starfall, an uncrewed capsule built to return cargo from orbit

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its Starfall Demo mission on Tuesday, June 23, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station aboard a Falcon 9, debuting a new uncrewed reentry capsule designed to bring cargo back from low-Earth orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off on Tuesday to test a new reentry vehicle designed to deliver cargo anywhere in the world from low-Earth orbit. The company developed the new saucer-shaped reentry pod, called Starfall, under a veil of secrecy.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX confirmed deployment of Starfall into low-Earth orbit; after demonstrating controlled flight, the spacecraft was expected to splash down in the Pacific Ocean.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX confirmed the deployment of Starfall into low-Earth orbit. The mission includes a demonstration of a new vehicle that will enable affordable, routine access to the microgravity environment... After demonstrating controlled flight, the spacecraft is expected to splash down in the Pacific Ocean.

key_facts.fact: According to FAA filings, the disk-shaped capsule, roughly 10 feet wide and 2.5 feet tall, is engineered to return up to 1,000 kilograms (2,200 pounds) of payload from orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: the capsule is roughly 10 feet wide and 2.5 feet tall. It is engineered specifically as a low-cost, mass-produced cargo vehicle capable of returning up to 2,200 pounds of payload back to Earth.

key_facts.fact: The capsule targets orbital manufacturing markets, allowing companies to make pharmaceuticals, semiconductors and optical materials in microgravity before returning them, as well as point-to-point cargo delivery through space.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX has previously said Starfall will enable cargo delivery from space, such as for manufactured materials in low Earth orbit like pharmaceutical compounds or semiconductor alloys.

key_facts.fact: The Falcon 9 first-stage booster made its 29th flight and landed on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas in the Atlantic; SpaceX has revealed little publicly, with most details drawn from FAA and FCC filings.
key_facts.excerpt: The flight utilized a highly experienced first-stage booster making its 29th flight... Following stage separation, the booster successfully completed its return to Earth, landing upright on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas.

key_facts.fact: The US military has signed agreements with Blue Origin, Rocket Lab and Anduril for cargo-delivery-from-space studies, and the Pentagon's Rocket Cargo program envisions using SpaceX's larger Starship for rapid deliveries.
key_facts.excerpt: The military has also signed agreements with Blue Origin, Rocket Lab, and Anduril for studies and development of technologies for global cargo delivery from space.

stories.headline: Takeda's zasocitinib beats deucravacitinib on skin clearance in Phase 3 psoriasis study

key_facts.fact: On June 23, Takeda announced positive topline results from a Phase 3 head-to-head study of zasocitinib (TAK-279), an investigational oral, highly selective TYK2 inhibitor, versus deucravacitinib in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
key_facts.excerpt: Takeda is pleased to announce positive topline results for the Phase 3, randomized, multicenter, double-blind study comparing zasocitinib (TAK-279), an investigational, next-generation, highly selective and potent oral tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitor, to deucravacitinib in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

key_facts.fact: In the LATITUDE Atlas study, zasocitinib demonstrated statistical superiority over deucravacitinib on the primary endpoint, the PASI 100 (complete skin clearance) response rate at week 16.
key_facts.excerpt: zasocitinib demonstrated statistical superiority over deucravacitinib for the primary endpoint, Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) 100 response rate at week 16.

key_facts.fact: The drug also showed statistical superiority on all key secondary endpoints, including PASI 90 response and a Static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) score of 0 at week 16.
key_facts.excerpt: The study also demonstrated statistical superiority over deucravacitinib for all key secondary endpoints, including PASI 90 response and Static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) 0 at week 16.

key_facts.fact: The study was conducted across eight countries and enrolled 606 participants; zasocitinib was generally well tolerated with no new safety signals identified.
key_facts.excerpt: Zasocitinib was generally well tolerated with a consistent safety and tolerability profile and no new safety signals identified. The study was conducted across eight countries and enrolled 606 participants.

key_facts.fact: Takeda said it is on track to submit a New Drug Application for plaque psoriasis to the FDA and other regulators starting this fiscal year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is on track to submit a New Drug Application for plaque psoriasis with the United States Food and Drug Administration and other regulatory authorities starting this fiscal year.

stories.headline: US and Iran clash over nuclear inspections after Switzerland technical talks conclude

key_facts.fact: Iran announced early Tuesday, June 23, that four-party technical talks with the US, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, concluded in Burgenstock, Switzerland, agreeing on arrangements for future negotiations including working groups and implementation mechanisms.
key_facts.excerpt: Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi, who led Iran's technical negotiating team, said the four-party talks concluded with an agreement on arrangements for future negotiations, including working groups and implementation mechanisms.

key_facts.fact: The parties agreed to establish four working groups covering sanctions removal, nuclear-related sanctions, reconstruction and economic development, and monitoring and implementation, under the framework of the June 17 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.
key_facts.excerpt: The parties agreed to establish four working groups dealing with sanctions removal, nuclear-related sanctions, reconstruction and economic development, and monitoring and implementation, he added.

key_facts.fact: A dispute broke out after the talks: Trump posted on Tuesday that Tehran had 'fully and completely agreed to (the) highest level Nuclear inspections,' but Iran's representative denied Iran had agreed to readmit IAEA inspectors, saying that would be addressed only in the next stage.
key_facts.excerpt: Bahreini denied that Iran had agreed to allow nuclear inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)... Trump responded later on Tuesday in a social media post, insisting that Tehran had 'fully and completely agreed to (the) highest level Nuclear inspections.'

key_facts.fact: Iran also rejected US Vice President JD Vance's claim that unfrozen Iranian assets would be used to buy US soybeans and wheat, with the Iranian ambassador saying Iran alone would decide how to use its funds.
key_facts.excerpt: The Iranian ambassador also rejected statements made by Vance that unfrozen Iranian assets would be used to purchase US soy and wheat products. 'Iran is the only country that will decide what to do with its assets.'

key_facts.fact: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, who led the negotiating team, said he walked out of Sunday's talks after Trump issued threats, arguing the remarks violated the first clause of the signed understanding prohibiting threats and the use of force.
key_facts.excerpt: 'I told Vance that we are here in talks and that the first clause of the signed understanding prohibits threats and the use of force. But your president issued threats today,' he said... 'We ended the talks, left the meeting and did not return.'

key_facts.fact: Mediators Qatar and Pakistan said the sides agreed on a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days, and the two governments established a direct communication line on the Strait of Hormuz to ensure safe passage for commercial vessels.
key_facts.excerpt: the talks produced a high-level committee to provide political oversight and working groups... and a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days. The United States and Iran also agreed to establish a direct communication channel to prevent incidents and misunderstandings in the Strait of Hormuz.
